facts.headline: The glass pyramid isn't cursed with 666 panes
facts.body_html: The Da Vinci Code made "666 panes" famous, but I.M. Pei's Louvre Pyramid actually has 673 glass panes — 603 diamonds and 70 triangles, confirmed by the architect's own team.

facts.headline: One chapel holds more stained glass than most cathedrals
facts.body_html: Sainte-Chapelle's 13th-century windows pack in 1,113 biblical scenes across 618 square meters of glass — and most survived WWII only because they were pulled out pane by pane and hidden.

facts.headline: The rooster on top of Notre-Dame is a reliquary
facts.body_html: Notre-Dame's gilded spire rooster secretly holds fragments of the Crown of Thorns. It survived the 2019 fire even as the spire collapsed beneath it.

facts.headline: A pendulum here proved the Earth spins
facts.body_html: In 1851, Léon Foucault hung a 28kg bob from a 67-meter wire under the Panthéon's dome — the first visual proof the planet rotates. You can still watch it swing today.

facts.headline: The Paris Opera House is built over a hidden lake
facts.body_html: Beneath Palais Garnier sits a 25x50 meter underground reservoir Charles Garnier built to fight groundwater — the real inspiration for Phantom of the Opera. Fire divers still train in it.

facts.headline: 6 million Parisians are stacked under the streets
facts.body_html: The Paris Catacombs hold the bones of roughly 6 million people — more than double the city's living population — packed into tunnels it took 12 years to fill.

facts.headline: This bookstore has hosted 30,000 free sleepovers
facts.body_html: Since 1951, over 30,000 traveling writers have slept for free among the shelves at Shakespeare and Company — in exchange for reading one book a day.
